summary: node1 now has a persistent firewalld policy permitting SSH and TCP/8080 while rejecting unrelated inbound connections. The RHEL 7.9 release and 3.10 kernel remain unchanged. Configuration and behavior survived a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Narrowed the public zone to SSH and TCP/8080.
Enabled persistent IPv4 and IPv6 rejection of unrelated inbound traffic.
Verified real TCP/8080 acceptance and TCP/8081 rejection from an isolated source namespace.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Reverified services, policy, kernel rules, and live behavior after restart.
Removed all temporary listeners, interfaces, and namespaces.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged across the work and restart.

evidence.requirement: Persistent host firewall permits SSH and TCP/8080
evidence.summary: firewalld is active and enabled; runtime and permanent policies contain SSH and 8080/tcp; generated IPv4 and IPv6 rules allow ports 22 and 8080.
With real listeners on both ports, TCP/8080 succeeded while TCP/8081 was rejected; firewall ACCEPT and REJECT counters recorded the respective traffic before and after restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf was captured, restart acknowledgement returned, boot ID changed to 7d7f58b9-6dd7-4e0f-87aa-2564020f3c0e, and firewall/SSH services, policy, rules, and behavior recovered.
firewalld and sshd are active, final allowed policy is ssh plus 8080/tcp, no failed units were reported, and no temporary test resources remain.
